title: Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome
note: Generated by tools/positions.py --extract from the page itself. Edit the verification, kind, signed_off_by and note fields; everything else is rewritten on the next extraction. positions.as_written: Take the history first, because the pattern carries this diagnosis: pain on stairs, on prolonged sitting, on squatting and after activity rather than during it.
Assess the patellar facets by displacing the patella and pressing on each.
Assess the painful arc actively and then with the patella compressed, which loads the joint specifically.
Assess the tracking in sitting and under load, since maltracking and dynamic valgus are the treatable contributors.
Exclude the alternatives deliberately: the meniscus, the ligaments, the tendons and the hip.
Assess the quadriceps and the proximal control, because both are what treatment changes.
Mechanical symptoms, an effusion or a positive meniscal test point away and should be pursued.
A patient whose pain has a mechanical component found on examination has a different diagnosis, and this label should not be applied to it.
In medicolegal work this diagnosis is difficult to attribute to an injury, because it has no structural correlate, and that limit should be stated plainly.
